content: Postoperative management should prioritize the prevention of vitamin and mineral deficiencies. This can be achieved through appropriate dietary modifications and the use of supplements tailored to the patient’s needs. Over time, patients may develop complications that manifest as symptoms such as nausea and fatigue, which require careful monitoring and intervention. It is strongly recommended that patients undergo lifelong follow-up care to maintain optimal nutritional health and to prevent metabolic imbalances that could arise after surgery. This follow-up care is essential to ensure long-term well-being and to address any emerging health concerns promptly. Specialized medical centers equipped with multidisciplinary teams of healthcare professionals are best suited to provide comprehensive care. These teams are trained to identify and manage potential risks associated with postoperative and long-term recovery, ensuring that patients receive the highest standard of care.
